newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 to push up near-term then fall.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 to push up near-term then fall.

text.p: The FTSE-100 index has enough momentum to inch higher in the short term, technical analysts said on Monday, but will come under pressure later in the week, relying on last Friday's low of 3,933.9 for ultimate support.
By 1035 GMT the blue chip index was up 17.5 at 3,989.9.
"The FTSE should push a little bit further in the short term," said Anne Whitby, technical analyst at 4CAST. "But I think it will come under pressure, probably not today but certainly into the week."
Whitby said the FTSE would come up against near-term resistance at 4,009.9, the high from December 12.
After that, more resistance kicks in at 4,035.70 and then the December 10 high of 4,043.2.
"Above that there's a whole load of congestion around 4,050. We've already got an overbought hourly RSI, so I'd have thought that would likely be the limit for the time being," she said.
Analysts said the fact the FTSE had not closed below the crucial 3,900 level was supportive, preventing a double top from forming which would signal the end of the bull run.
Whitby said Friday's high of 3,972.4 would provided a prop for the market should it begin to slide, with congestion around 3,959 to 3,950 giving further support.
"Below that, Friday's low of 3933.9 ought to be the limit of any correction," she said.
